page: JWK Auth Middleware for JWT authentication using JSON Web Keys. Import: {Hono} from 'hono', {jwk} from 'hono/jwk', {verifyWithJwks} from 'hono/jwt'. Validates JWT header format, kid header match, asymmetric algorithms only, alg allowlist, signature. Default claims validated: nbf, exp, iat. Optional: iss, aud claims. HTTP header: Authorization with scheme (Bearer, Basic required). HTTP status: 401 Unauthorized. Access payload: c.get('jwtPayload'). Algorithms supported: RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384, ES512, EdDSA. Rejects symmetric algorithms (HS256, HS384, HS512). Options: alg (required, array), keys (optional, array or function), jwks_uri (optional, string or function), allow_anon (optional, boolean), cookie (optional, name), headerName (optional, default 'Authorization'), realm (optional, default request URL), verification (optional, VerifyOptions for iss, aud, nbf, iat, exp). verifyWithJwks utility for non-Hono contexts (SvelteKit SSR). RequestInit second argument for JWKS fetch options. Cloudflare caching support. Questions: How to verify JWTs? Which algorithms are supported? How to use JWKS URI? Can I allow anonymous? How to access payload? What claims are checked? How to use outside Hono? Can I customize headers? What about issuer/audience validation?

sections.manifest: JWK Auth Middleware validation checks performed on each token. Parses and validates JWT header format. Requires kid (key ID) header and finds matching key by kid. Rejects symmetric algorithms (HS256, HS384, HS512). Requires header alg to be in configured alg allowlist (RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384, ES512, EdDSA). If JWK has alg field, must match JWT header alg. Verifies token signature with matched key. Default time-based claim validation: nbf (not before), exp (expiration), iat (issued at). Optional claim validation via verification option: iss (issuer), aud (audience). Authorization header format: must include scheme prefix like 'Bearer token' or 'Basic token'. Additional custom authorization checks must be added in separate middleware after jwk(). Questions: What validations are performed? Why kid header required? Why reject symmetric algorithms? Which claims are checked? Can I skip claim validation? What header format is needed?

Import statements for JWK Auth. import {Hono} from 'hono' for main framework. import {jwk} from 'hono/jwk' for middleware. import {verifyWithJwks} from 'hono/jwt' for utility function. Questions: What to import? Where are these located?

JWK Auth middleware usage patterns. Pattern 1: Basic with jwks_uri. jwk({jwks_uri: 'https://server/.well-known/jwks.json', alg: ['RS256']}). Pattern 2: Get payload. const payload = c.get('jwtPayload'). Returns decoded token claims like {sub, name, iat}. Pattern 3: Anonymous access. jwk({jwks_uri: (c) => 'https://${c.env.authServer}/.well-known/jwks.json', alg: ['RS256'], allow_anon: true}). Allow requests without valid token, check c.get('jwtPayload') for auth status. Pattern 4: jwks_uri as function for dynamic URI. jwks_uri: (c) => string from context. Questions: How to set up basic auth? How to get token payload? What does allow_anon do? Can jwks_uri be dynamic? What's the payload format?

verifyWithJwks utility function for JWT verification outside Hono. Used in SvelteKit SSR pages and non-Hono server contexts. Signature: await verifyWithJwks(token, options, fetchOptions). Parameters: token (JWT string), options {jwks_uri, allowedAlgorithms}, fetchOptions (RequestInit). Returns: decoded payload. Supports Cloudflare caching: {cf: {cacheEverything: true, cacheTtl: 3600}}. Example: const id_payload = await verifyWithJwks(token, {jwks_uri: 'https://...', allowedAlgorithms: ['RS256']}, {cf: {...}}). Questions: When to use verifyWithJwks? What environments support it? How to pass options? Can I cache JWKS? What does the function return?

JWKS fetch request configuration via second jwk() argument. Second argument to jwk(): RequestInit object. Applied only to JWKS fetch request, not token verification. Example: jwk({...}, {headers: {Authorization: 'Bearer TOKEN'}}). Can set custom headers, timeout, method, body, etc. Allows authentication for private JWKS endpoints. Pattern: jwk(options, fetchRequestInit). Questions: How to configure JWKS fetch? What's RequestInit? Can I add headers? When needed? What about timeouts?

JWK Auth middleware options specification. Required: alg (AsymmetricAlgorithm[] array, allowed algorithms: RS256, RS384, RS512, PS256, PS384, PS512, ES256, ES384, ES512, EdDSA). Optional: keys (HonoJsonWebKey[] array or (c: Context) => Promise<HonoJsonWebKey[]> function for public keys). Optional: jwks_uri (string or (c: Context) => Promise<string> function, fetches keys from URI with 'keys' field, combined with keys option). Optional: allow_anon (boolean, default false, allows requests without valid token). Optional: cookie (string, cookie name for token extraction). Optional: headerName (string, default 'Authorization', header name for token). Optional: realm (string, default request URL, WWW-Authenticate header protection space). Optional: verification (VerifyOptions for claim validation). VerifyOptions: iss (string | RegExp for issuer validation), aud (string | string[] | RegExp for audience), nbf (boolean, default true), iat (boolean, default true), exp (boolean, default true). Questions: Which options required? What are defaults? How to provide keys? Can I use both keys and jwks_uri? How to validate claims? Can I customize headers?
